info.description:
Welcome to the CloudQuery Platform API documentation! This API can be used to interact with the CloudQuery platform. As a user, the API allows you to search the CloudQuery asset inventory, run SQL queries against the data warehouse, save and load searches, and much more. As an administrator, it allows you to manage your teams, syncs, and other objects.
### Authentication
The API is secured using bearer tokens. To get started, you can generate an API key for your Platform deployment from your platform dashboard. For a step-by-step guide, see: https://www.cloudquery.io/docs/cli/managing-cloudquery/deployments/generate-api-key.
The base URL for the API depends on where your CloudQuery Platform is hosted. If running locally, this is usually http://localhost:3000/api. In a production deployment it should be an HTTPS URL. For purposes of illustration, we will assume the platform instance is available at https://cloudquery.mycompany.com. In this case, the base API endpoint will be https://cloudquery.mycompany.com/api.
### Example Request
To test your connection to the API, we can use the `/plugins` endpoint. For example:
`curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDQUERY_API_KEY" \ https://cloudquery.mycompany.com/api/plugins`

post.description: Mint a short-lived (~7 days), signed platform-destination token (prefix `cqpd_`) for the caller's tenant. The user pastes this token as their CloudQuery CLI credential: it authenticates plugin/usage calls to cloud (which verifies it offline) and `/external-syncs/*` on this platform — no host configuration. Any signed-in tenant user with write access can mint one for their own tenant, whatever their login method (local password, SAML, magic link); a tenant API key with write access works too, for CI (a default `ci`-role key cannot mint). It is a derived credential: the CLI re-mints it from the durable root (cloud login, a tenant API key, or a fresh tenant sign-in) as it nears expiry, so a leaked token expires within about a week. There is no per-token revocation — verification is offline on both stacks, against either of the tenant's two external-sync secret slots. Rotating the secret demotes the outgoing one to the second slot as a grace window, so outstanding tokens keep working until a second rotation displaces it; two rotations revoke every outstanding token for the tenant. Disabling the user who minted a token does not invalidate it before it expires. Returned once.

get.description:
List the tenant-global default notification rules, in evaluation order. Same shape as an insight's list; this is the tier a resource falls through to when the insight's own list leaves it unmatched. A tenant with no global rules returns 200 with an empty `rules` list rather than 404.

This tier supersedes `PUT /notifications/defaults/{type}` for insight alerts. While notification rules v2 is enabled for the tenant, these rules are the only routing input; the v1 default-destination rows stay readable and writable, are what the pre-v2 path uses, and have already been carried into this list by the one-time migration - so a v1 write after that point does not change v2 routing.

put.description:
Replace the whole tenant-global default rule list. Identical semantics to the per-insight PUT: the array index becomes `ord`, the server reconciles by rule ID, and a rule missing from the list is deleted along with its per-resource notification state. Because it is the delete mechanism for every tenant-wide default at once, it requires the same admin write access as `PUT /notifications/defaults/{type}`.

Send the write shape, not the read shape: `ord`, `created_at` and `updated_at` are server-assigned and rejected on the way in.

400 is returned when an unconditional rule is not last, more than one rule is unconditional, a condition type is unknown, an `app` condition's values are not app IDs, a `tag` condition has no `key` or a non-tag condition carries one, a `destination_id` names no destination, a template is sent alongside `body_format: structured` (the structured envelope is built from the event, so the template would never be sent), a template exceeds 32 KB, a `liquid` webhook template's sample render does not produce valid JSON, a `subject` is sent for a destination that is not email, an email row carries only one of `subject` and `template`, or a subject is over 1 KB, has a line break or does not render. 403 is an insufficient role.

get.description:
Get the candidate values for the next filter dimension (`column_name`), given the current active filters. The supplied filter parameters represent where the user currently is in the filter matrix; only values for `column_name` that would yield at least one insight when added to that current position are returned. Values that would produce zero results are omitted, preventing the user from navigating to an empty state.
The filter parameter corresponding to `column_name` is always ignored when computing candidates — asking "which severities exist where severity=X" is self-referential and nonsensical. For example, if `column_name=severity` then any `severities` filter in the request is not applied; if `column_name=source` then any `source` filter is not applied; and so on. This ensures the full set of viable values for that dimension is always returned given the other active filters.
When `owner_tag` is specified (e.g., "team", "department"), this endpoint returns distinct values for that specific ownership tag key, ignoring the `column_name` parameter. The corresponding tags filter for this owner key is ignored to prevent self-referential queries.
When querying for `column_name=tag` without `owner_tag`, ownership tags configured in platform settings are automatically excluded from results.

Rules are first-match-wins per affected resource; a resource the list leaves unmatched - possible only when the list has no unconditional rule - continues into the tenant-global default list. An insight with no rules of its own returns 200 with an empty `rules` list rather than 404, which is also how "inherits the global default" is represented, so callers can read uniformly.

put.description:
Replace the whole rule list for one insight. The array index becomes each rule's `ord`, so this is also the reorder call. The server reconciles by rule ID - a rule whose ID is echoed back is updated in place, one with no ID is created, and one missing from the list is deleted along with its per-resource notification state. Edits take effect at the next evaluation cycle; nothing is evaluated at save.

400 is returned when an unconditional rule is not last, more than one rule is unconditional, a condition type is unknown, an `app` condition's values are not app IDs, a `tag` condition has no `key` or a non-tag condition carries one, a `destination_id` names no destination, a template is sent alongside `body_format: structured` (the structured envelope is built from the event, so the template would never be sent), a template exceeds 32 KB, a `liquid` webhook template's sample render does not produce valid JSON, a `subject` is sent for a destination that is not email, an email row carries only one of `subject` and `template`, or a subject is over 1 KB, has a line break or does not render. 403 is an insufficient role.

get.description:
Walk the `shared/topology` corpus outgoing from the given source row,
returning related rows grouped by target resource type. Each outgoing
edge at salience >= floor (primary + secondary) is executed against the
source row; rows from multiple edges into the same target table are
coalesced into one group and deduplicated by `_cq_platform_id`. Per-edge
errors are logged server-side and do not abort the request.

Each group carries a `via` array. The array names the edges that the
walk used for that group, with the relationship verb, the direction
and the weight. A consumer can then say how a resource is related,
and not only that it is related. An edge that matched no rows is
still named.

A few corpus nodes hold an event stream rather than an inventory of
resources — AWS CloudTrail events, GCP audit logs. A walk into one of
these reads the last `window_days` days and no more. Each `via` entry
for such an edge carries a `time_bound` that names the window that ran.

The window never applies to the row named in the path. Asking about one
event returns what that event touched, however old the event is: one row
read by its id is not a scan, so there is nothing to narrow.

This endpoint supersedes `POST /tables/{table_name}/related-resources`
by walking the topology corpus instead of hand-curated relation
templates under `api/relations/configs/`.

Event-stream neighbours such as CloudTrail events are limited to the last window_days days, 7 by default and up to 30; ask for more and you get 30. Get Table Column Values.

Values always come from the physical column the requested name resolves to, so `filter_mode` is accepted for compatibility and ignored: one column returns one set of values in every mode.

The reserved column name `_cq_owner` returns the distinct owners the tenant's ownership rules resolved, read from `resource_ownership` rather than from a physical column, so the `_cq_owner` filter has a value list. Resources no rule claimed contribute nothing; filter those with `_cq_owner IS EMPTY`.

Group rows of a table by the distinct non-empty values of a column and return one item per group with an exact row count. Used by the asset inventory's Group-by selector. Always runs in column-filter mode because exact per-row counts cannot be produced from the search index.

The reserved column name `apps` groups by app membership instead of a physical column: each item is an app with its `app_id`, resolved `title`, `owner_name` and a distinct-resource `count`, plus a synthetic `is_unallocated` bucket for resources in no app. Counts honor any `filter` arguments, so the grouping reflects the currently filtered resource set.

The reserved column name `_cq_owner` groups by resolved resource owner instead of a physical column: each item is an owner string with a distinct-resource `count`, plus a synthetic `is_unowned` bucket for resources no ownership rule claimed. Counts honor any `filter` arguments, and an active `_cq_owner` filter also pins which owners are returned.

The reserved column name `_cq_environment` groups by the environment the tenant's environment identification rules named, instead of a physical column: each item is an environment name with a distinct-resource `count`, plus a synthetic `is_unclassified` bucket for resources no rule named. Counts honor any `filter` arguments, and an active `_cq_environment` filter also pins which environments are returned.

PlatformAppListItem.title: AppListItem
PlatformAppListItem.description: One entry in the `GET /apps` response. Always includes a resolved display `title` (server-side COALESCE of the stored title with the underlying name) and a `resource_count`. The last entry in the list is the synthetic "unallocated" pseudo-app (`is_unallocated_resources: true`), which has a null `id` and represents resources not currently in any app.

id.description: The app's id. Null for the synthetic unallocated entry; a real UUID for every other row.

owner_team_name.description: Free-form team-ownership label. Null for the synthetic unallocated entry.

owner_team_names.description: Owners inferred for the app from its member resources, distinct and sorted. Written by each app-membership recompute, so it is derived and not editable through this API, and it is empty for a tenant whose ownership configuration resolves no owner. Holds the same values as `derived_owners`, which is read live from the warehouse instead; this column is the stored copy, so a caller that only needs the owners does not pay for that read. Separate from the hand-set `owner_team_name`, which no inference overwrites. Capped at 50 entries, the same cap `derived_owners` carries. A truncated list here is the first 50 in sort order, not the arbitrary sample `derived_owners` returns, so it does not change between recomputes. Read `derived_owner_count` for the true total.

derived_owners.description: Owners derived from the app's resources by the tenant's resource-ownership rules, distinct and sorted. Independent of the manually-set `owner_team_name`: both are returned and it is the caller's choice which to render. Empty when no member resource resolved to an owner, when the tenant configured no ownership rules, and always for the synthetic unallocated entry. Capped at 50 entries, because owner values come from tenant-controlled tag values and SQL columns and are not a bounded set of team names; read `derived_owner_count` for the true total and treat a count above the array length as a truncated list. The items are an arbitrary sample, not the first 50 of the ordering.

derived_owner_count.description: How many distinct owners the app's resources resolved to, counted before the `derived_owners` cap is applied. Equal to the length of that array unless the list was truncated. Zero for an app with no owned resources and for the synthetic unallocated entry.

resource_count.description: Number of distinct resources currently attributed to this app. For the synthetic unallocated entry, this is the count of warehouse resources that are not in any app.

is_unallocated_resources.description: True for the synthetic entry that represents resources not in any app. Exactly one entry in the response has this flag set.

PlatformAppsListResponse.title: AppsListResponse
PlatformAppsListResponse.description: Apps for the caller's tenant. Real apps are listed first, ordered by case-insensitive display title. The synthetic unallocated entry is appended last.

PlatformAppCriticality.title: AppCriticality
PlatformAppCriticality.description: User-assigned business criticality of an app. Free metadata (does not affect identification); surfaced in the asset inventory. Defaults to `standard`.

PlatformAppIdentificationRuleKind.title: AppIdentificationRuleKind
PlatformAppIdentificationRuleKind.description: The kind of an app-identification rule. `tag` derives an app name from configured resource-tag values. `account_name_pattern` derives it from a resource's account name via a regular expression with a named capture group. `envzero_environment` derives the name from the env0 environment that deployed the resource, and `envzero_project` from the env0 project that deployed it (see `envzero_project_naming`); both are matched via env0's synced state resources and carry no other configuration. See GET /apps/membership-policies/catalog for the kinds available to a tenant.

PlatformAppIdentificationRule.title: AppIdentificationRule
PlatformAppIdentificationRule.description: One rule in the ordered app-identification flow. Rules are evaluated in array order and the first one that yields an app name for a resource wins (later rules are not applied to that resource). The fields present depend on `kind`: a `tag` rule carries `tag_keys`; an `account_name_pattern` rule carries `regex`; an `envzero_project` rule carries `envzero_project_naming`; an `envzero_environment` rule carries no configuration fields.

enabled.description: Whether this rule participates in evaluation. A disabled rule is retained (so its config survives a round-trip) but skipped during matching.

tag_keys.description: For `tag` rules: resource-tag keys whose values name an app, in priority order. Evaluated first-match-wins within the rule — the first key a resource carries assigns its app. Keys are de-duplicated server-side, preserving order. May be empty (the rule then matches nothing). Must be absent for non-`tag` rules.

value_filters.description: For `tag` rules: an optional allow-list of tag values. When non-empty, a resource is attributed by this rule only if its matched tag value equals one of these entries (compared case-insensitively); when empty or absent, any value matches. The derived app name is still the resource's own tag value, so this narrows which resources the rule claims without changing the names it produces. Entries are de-duplicated server-side (case-insensitively), preserving order. Must be absent for non-`tag` rules.

regex.description: For `account_name_pattern` rules: a Go (RE2) regular expression matched against a resource's account name. It must contain a named capture group `app` (e.g. `^(?P<app>[a-z]+)-prod$`); the captured value names the app. Must be absent for non-pattern rules.

envzero_project_naming.description: For `envzero_project` rules: what the app is named after. `full_path` (the default) uses the whole project breadcrumb, so a project C inside B inside A becomes the app `A/B/C`. `leaf` uses only the project the environment lives in, so the same project becomes the app `C` — note that two projects sharing a name under different parents then merge into one app. Must be absent for other kinds.

propagate_to_untagged_neighbors.description: Whether a resource this rule anchors also propagates its app to directly connected, untagged neighbours (one hop out through the resource topology). When true (the default), the anchor's immediate neighbours are attributed to the same app; when false, only the anchor resource itself is attributed. Omitted/null is treated as true, so policies saved before this field existed keep propagating. Applies to both `tag` and `account_name_pattern` rules.

Optional initial extension `rules` may be supplied and are validated the same way as PUT /apps/{app_id}/membership-policy.

owner_team_name.description: Free-form team-ownership label. No referential link to a teams table.

PlatformAppSource.title: AppSource

PlatformApp.title: App
PlatformApp.description: An app — a named grouping of resources within a tenant. `name` is the canonical machine identifier (set by the post-sync accessory from resource tag values); `title` and `owner_team_name` are user-editable display fields.

id.description: The unique ID of an app.

name.description: Canonical, immutable identifier, unique within a tenant. For `auto` apps it is set when the app is first upserted from a resource-tag value; for `custom` apps it is set from the `title` at creation. Distinct from `title`, which is the user-editable display string.

rules.description: Extension rules for a `custom` app: additive selectors that attribute more resources to this app (the app name is fixed — it is not derived from the matched value, unlike the org-wide policy). Empty/absent for `auto` apps.

title.description: User-editable display label for the app. Optional; when unset, callers typically render `name`.

owner_team_name.description: Free-form team-ownership label for the app. No referential link to a teams table.

owner_team_names.description: Owners inferred for the app from its member resources, distinct and sorted. Written by each app-membership recompute, so it is derived and not editable through this API, and it is empty for a tenant whose ownership configuration resolves no owner. Holds the same values as `derived_owners`, which is read live from the warehouse instead; this column is the stored copy, so a caller that only needs the owners does not pay for that read. Separate from the hand-set `owner_team_name`, which no inference overwrites. Capped at 50 entries, the same cap `derived_owners` carries. A truncated list here is the first 50 in sort order, not the arbitrary sample `derived_owners` returns, so it does not change between recomputes. Read `derived_owner_count` for the true total.

owner_contact.description: Free-form owner contact (e.g. an email or Slack handle). Metadata only.

derived_owners.description: Owners derived from the app's resources by the tenant's resource-ownership rules, distinct and sorted, matching `derived_owners` on `AppListItem`. Independent of the manually-set `owner_team_name`: both are returned and it is the caller's choice which to render. Capped at 50 entries; read `derived_owner_count` for the true total. Empty on a just-created app, whose resources are attributed by the next recompute.

derived_owner_count.description: How many distinct owners the app's resources resolved to, counted before the `derived_owners` cap is applied.

Sent as the body of PUT /apps/{app_id}/membership-policy and replaces the app's current rules wholesale.

PlatformAppMembershipPolicyPreview.title: AppMembershipPolicyPreview
PlatformAppMembershipPolicyPreview.description: The read-only projection of applying a candidate app-identification policy to the caller's current warehouse state (nothing is persisted). Reports, per rule, how many resources the rule would classify.

total_resources_classified.description: The number of distinct resources the whole policy would attribute to at least one app. A resource reachable by more than one rule or app is counted once here.

rules.description: Per-rule projection, index-aligned with the request policy's `rules` array (same length and order); a disabled or empty rule reports zero. Anchors are first-match-wins (each anchor resource counts for one rule), but a propagated neighbour reachable from two rules under different apps is counted for each, so per-rule counts may overlap and can sum to more than total_resources_classified.

total_resources_classified_by_environmen.description: The number of distinct resources the policy's `environment_rules` would attribute to at least one environment. Counted independently of total_resources_classified (a resource can be attributed to both an app and an environment). Zero when the candidate policy has no environment rules.

environment_rules.description: Per-rule projection for the candidate policy's `environment_rules`, index-aligned with that array (same length and order); a disabled or empty rule reports zero. Empty when the candidate policy has no environment rules.

PlatformEnvironmentIdentificationRule.title: EnvironmentIdentificationRule
PlatformEnvironmentIdentificationRule.description: One rule in the ordered environment-identification flow. Structurally the twin of AppIdentificationRule but it names an environment (dev/staging/prod/...) rather than an app: rules are evaluated in array order and the first one that yields an environment name for a resource wins (later rules are not applied to that resource). The fields present depend on `kind`: a `tag` rule carries `tag_keys`; an `account_name_pattern` rule carries `regex`; an `envzero_environment` rule carries no configuration fields — it attributes a resource to the env0 environment that deployed it (matched by the provider-native resource id env0 records in its state resources); an `envzero_project` rule names the environment after that environment's env0 project and carries `envzero_project_naming`.

enabled.description: Whether this rule participates in evaluation. A disabled rule is retained (so its config survives a round-trip) but skipped during matching.

tag_keys.description: For `tag` rules: resource-tag keys whose values name an environment, in priority order. Evaluated first-match-wins within the rule — the first key a resource carries assigns its environment. Keys are de-duplicated server-side, preserving order. May be empty (the rule then matches nothing). Must be absent for non-`tag` rules.

value_filters.description: For `tag` rules: an optional allow-list of tag values. When non-empty, a resource is attributed by this rule only if its matched tag value equals one of these entries (compared case-insensitively); when empty or absent, any value matches. The derived environment name is still the resource's own tag value, so this narrows which resources the rule claims without changing the names it produces. Entries are de-duplicated server-side (case-insensitively), preserving order. Must be absent for non-`tag` rules.

regex.description: For `account_name_pattern` rules: a Go (RE2) regular expression matched against a resource's account name. It must contain a named capture group `environment` (e.g. `^[a-z]+-(?P<environment>dev|staging|prod)$`); the captured value names the environment. Must be absent for non-pattern rules.

envzero_project_naming.description: For `envzero_project` rules: what the environment is named after. `full_path` (the default) uses the whole project breadcrumb, so a project C inside B inside A becomes the environment `A/B/C`. `leaf` uses only the project the env0 environment lives in, so the same project becomes the environment `C` — note that two projects sharing a name under different parents then merge into one environment. Must be absent for other kinds.

propagate_to_untagged_neighbors.description: Whether a resource this rule anchors also propagates its environment to directly connected, untagged neighbours (one hop out through the resource topology). When true (the default), the anchor's immediate neighbours are attributed to the same environment; when false, only the anchor resource itself is attributed. Omitted/null is treated as true, matching AppIdentificationRule. Applies to both `tag` and `account_name_pattern` rules.

PlatformAppMembershipPolicy.title: AppMembershipPolicy
PlatformAppMembershipPolicy.description: The app-identification policy for the caller's tenant: an ordered list of rules that decide which resources belong to which app. A per-tenant singleton, read via GET /apps/membership-policy and replaced via PUT. Rules are evaluated in order, first-match-wins. When unset the default is an empty rule set (`{rules: []}`) — identification is opt-in, so an unconfigured tenant identifies nothing.

rules.description: The ordered app-identification rules. Evaluated in array order; the first rule that yields an app name for a resource wins. May be empty (identifies nothing, clearing the tenant's memberships on the next recompute).

environment_rules.description: The ordered environment-identification rules, evaluated independently of `rules` and in the same first-match-wins fashion (the first rule that yields an environment name for a resource wins). Optional; an absent or empty list identifies no environments. Environment inference is configured here but applied by a separate recompute (see ATH-85).

PlatformAppMembershipRecomputeStatus.title: AppMembershipRecomputeStatus
PlatformAppMembershipRecomputeStatus.description: Progress of the background app-membership recompute for the caller's tenant. The frontend polls this after changing the membership policy to know when the new rules have been fully materialized.

state.description: `running` while a recompute is queued or in progress. The recompute keeps its job running until the tenant's latest policy is fully materialized, so `idle` is reported only once the current policy is what's visible — never before convergence.

last_completed_at.description: When the most recent recompute finished successfully, if any.

last_error.description: The error from the most recent recompute that exhausted its retries, if the last run failed.

PlatformInferenceSignalAccount.description: One account's resource count, with the display name a naming-convention rule would match on.

account_name.description: The account's display name, or empty when the provider mapping does not populate one. An empty value here is the signal that a naming-convention rule has nothing to match on for this account.

cloud.description: The provider this account belongs to, e.g. `aws`, `gcp`, `azure`.

PlatformInferenceSignalTagValue.title: InferenceSignalTagValue
PlatformInferenceSignalTagValue.description: One value observed under a tag key, with how many resources carry it.

PlatformInferenceSignalTagKey.title: InferenceSignalTagKey
PlatformInferenceSignalTagKey.description: One tag key's shape across the resources in scope.

key.description: One entry per key, not per casing: `Owner` and `owner` are one key here because a rule naming either claims the same resources. Shown in the spelling most of the tenant's resources use.

resources_with_value.description: Resources carrying a non-blank value. Against `total_resources` this is coverage — a key on 2% of the estate makes a rule that claims 2% of it.

distinct_values.description: Distinct non-blank values. Read it against `resources_with_value`, because both extremes disqualify the key: as many values as resources means an id or a name, and exactly one value means every resource would get the same owner, which is a static rule wearing a per-resource costume.

distinct_value_shapes.description:
Distinct values after digits are collapsed, so `web-1` and `web-2` count once.

This is not a verdict on the key. Numeric values are often meaningful — a billing code or an account number collapses to one shape and is still a good grouping. What it tells you is whether `top_values` is representative: one shape means the samples describe every value the key holds, and as many shapes as values means they describe almost none of them.

The case worth catching is a key whose distinct-value count looks healthy and is really a timestamp. One production key holds 223 values over 3,789 resources and exactly one shape; nothing in the counts alone would have shown that.

email_shaped_resources.description: Resources whose value looks like an email address. High against `resources_with_value` means the key names individuals; zero on a well-covered key means it names teams, environments or something else entirely.

selected_by.description: Why this key is in the response. `coverage` is the top-ranked set. `name` means the key name reads like ownership (owner, team, contact, maintainer, squad) and it is included regardless of rank — the key literally called `owner` is often far down the coverage order. `requested` means the caller named it in `tag_key`.

top_values.description:
The most common values, count descending then value ascending, capped by `tag_values_limit`. Values longer than 120 characters are truncated with a trailing ellipsis.

On a resource carrying two non-blank casings of one key with different values — rare, and only seen on AWS — one casing is counted and the other dropped, so a listed value may not be the one the resulting rule assigns to that resource.

PlatformInferenceSignals.title: InferenceSignals
PlatformInferenceSignals.description: What the resources in scope offer an ownership, app or environment inference rule to match on. Read-only; nothing is persisted.

total_resources.description: Distinct resources in scope — the whole tenant, or only the unowned ones when `unowned_only` is set. The denominator for every coverage judgement below.

resources_with_account_name.description: Resources carrying a non-blank `account_name`. Zero means no naming-convention rule is possible here yet, which is a different answer from an empty `accounts` list.

total_accounts.description: Accounts in scope, before `account_limit` truncates the list. One tenant in production has close to twelve thousand, so treat a large number as a reason to judge the convention from the sample rather than to page through.

total_tag_keys.description: Tag keys matching the request, before `tag_key_limit` truncates the list. When this exceeds the returned count, narrow with `key_search` or name keys in `tag_key` rather than assuming the rest are uninteresting.

hidden_named_tag_keys.description: Ownership-named keys dropped because that lane is bounded too. One production tenant carries twelve owner-ish keys under a single prefix, so the lane cannot be unlimited; a non-zero value here means narrow with `key_search` to see the rest.

accounts.description: Accounts by resource count descending then account ascending, capped by `account_limit`.

tag_keys.description: Tag keys: the top `tag_key_limit` by covered resources, plus every ownership-named key, plus anything named in `tag_key`. Each carries `selected_by` saying which. Only keys with at least one non-blank value appear.

PlatformOwnershipRuleKind.title: OwnershipRuleKind
PlatformOwnershipRuleKind.description: The kind of a resource-ownership rule. `static` assigns a fixed owner string to every resource that no higher-priority rule matched; because it matches every resource, rules ordered after it are never reached. `sql` runs the tenant's own query and joins its result onto matching resources. `tags` reads the owner from a resource's own tags, using the first of the rule's tag keys that the resource carries.

PlatformOwnershipRule.title: OwnershipRule
PlatformOwnershipRule.description: One rule in the ordered resource-ownership flow. Rules are evaluated in array order and the first one that yields an owner for a resource wins (later rules are not applied to that resource). The fields present depend on `kind`: a `static` rule carries `owner`, a `sql` rule carries `query`, a `tags` rule carries `tagKeys`.

id.description: Stable identifier for this rule. Assigned by the server when a rule is first saved without one; clients must send it back on subsequent PUTs so rows produced by the rule keep referring to it across edits and reordering. A PUT that omits it creates a new identity for the rule.

name.description: A label for this rule, shown in the rules UI so that several rules of the same kind can be told apart and reordered. Free text: not unique, not an identifier, and ignored entirely by matching and evaluation. Optional; a rule without one is shown by its kind.

enabled.description: Whether this rule participates in evaluation. A disabled rule is retained (so its config survives a round-trip) but skipped during matching.

owner.description: For `static` rules: the owner string assigned to every resource this rule matches. Must be non-blank for an enabled `static` rule. Must be absent for other kinds.

query.description: For `sql` rules: a single SELECT against any CloudQuery-ingested table. It must return exactly one column named `owner` plus at least one other column, and every other column must be one the platform can match resources on (see `matchColumns`). The platform joins the query result to the matching resources itself — the query does not join to `cloud_assets`. Must be absent for other kinds.

tagKeys.description: For `tags` rules: the tag keys to read the owner from, in priority order. A resource is owned by the value of the first of these keys it carries. Key matching is case-insensitive, so `owner` claims a resource tagged `Owner`; where a resource carries several case variants of one key, an exact-case match wins and otherwise the choice is stable but arbitrary. Tags with an empty value are ignored. Must be non-empty for an enabled `tags` rule, and absent for other kinds.

matchColumns.description: For `sql` rules: the non-`owner` columns the query returns, which are the columns the platform will join resources on. Server-computed by running the query's column list against the warehouse; ignored on write. Lets the rule form show what the rule joins on before it is saved.

PlatformResourceOwnershipPolicy.title: ResourceOwnershipPolicy
PlatformResourceOwnershipPolicy.description: The resource-ownership policy for the caller's tenant: an ordered list of rules that resolve each resource to an owner. A per-tenant singleton, read via GET /resources/ownership-policy and replaced via PUT. Rules are evaluated in order, first-match-wins. When unset, the default is the tenant's `ownership_tags` data setting as one `tags` rule, or an empty rule set (`{rules: []}`) when that setting is empty too. Ownership is opt-in, so an unconfigured tenant owns nothing.

rules.description: The ordered ownership rules. Evaluated in array order; the first rule that yields an owner for a resource wins. May be empty (owns nothing, clearing the tenant's resource ownership on the next recompute).

PlatformResourceOwnershipPolicyPreviewOw.title: ResourceOwnershipPolicyPreviewOwner
PlatformResourceOwnershipPolicyPreviewOw.description: One owner's projected resource count, within a single rule's claim or across the whole policy depending on where it appears.

owner.description: The owner value. For a `static` rule this is the rule's configured owner; for `tags` and `sql` rules it comes from the data, which is what makes this breakdown worth showing before saving.

resource_count.description: Distinct resources that would be attributed to this owner.

PlatformResourceOwnershipPolicyPreviewSa.title: ResourceOwnershipPolicyPreviewSample
PlatformResourceOwnershipPolicyPreviewSa.description: One illustrative resource a rule would claim.

resource_name.description: The resource's `name` as the plugin reported it, so a preview row can be recognised without looking it up. Empty where the plugin reports no name.

resource_table.description: The plugin table the resource came from, e.g. `aws_ec2_instances`.

owner.description: The owner this rule would resolve for this resource.

PlatformResourceOwnershipPolicyPreviewRu.title: ResourceOwnershipPolicyPreviewRule
PlatformResourceOwnershipPolicyPreviewRu.description: The projected claim for a single rule in an ownership-policy preview.

resource_count.description: Distinct resources this rule would own under the full ordered policy. Rules are a priority cascade, so this is the count AFTER the rules above have taken theirs — not what the rule would claim on its own.

owner_count.description: Distinct owners this rule would resolve. Not truncated, so a client showing only the top few can say how many more the rule matched.

owners.description: Per-owner breakdown of this rule's resources, ordered by count descending then owner ascending, capped at 100. A single tags or sql rule can yield many owners, so read the policy-wide `owners` rather than summing these.

sample_matches.description: Up to `max_samples` example resources this rule would claim. Empty or null when `max_samples` is 0. Ordered deterministically (by owner, then platform_id).

unreachable.description: True when this rule is ordered after a `static` rule. A static rule claims every resource left unclaimed, so nothing below it is ever evaluated. This is the ordering mistake the preview exists to catch, and it is distinct from a rule that ran and matched nothing.

skip_reason.description: Why this rule could not run, when it could not. A `sql` rule whose query fails to describe, validate or execute is skipped by the recompute, which keeps the previous ownership rather than clearing it. Empty when the rule ran.

PlatformResourceOwnershipPolicyPreviewAp.title: ResourceOwnershipPolicyPreviewApp
PlatformResourceOwnershipPolicyPreviewAp.description: What a candidate policy would mean for one app: how much of it ends up owned, by whom, and through which rules.

app_name.description: The app's name as `app_catalog` holds it. Empty when the app has a membership row but no catalog entry, which a recompute repairs.

resources_total.description: Distinct resources in the app, owned or not.

resources_owned.description: Distinct resources in the app the policy would give an owner.

owners.description: Distinct owners the policy resolves within the app, sorted, capped at 20. More than one means the app's resources disagree about who owns them.

matched_rules.description: Indexes into the request policy's `rules` array for the rules that claimed any of this app's resources, ascending. Empty when nothing claimed them.

PlatformResourceOwnershipPolicyPreview.title: ResourceOwnershipPolicyPreview
PlatformResourceOwnershipPolicyPreview.description: The read-only projection of applying a candidate resource-ownership policy to the caller's current warehouse state. Nothing is persisted and the tenant's saved policy is untouched.

total_resources_owned.description: Distinct resources the whole policy would own. Rules are a priority cascade in which each resource is claimed at most once. Counted before any per-rule truncation, so it can exceed the per-rule counts summed.

owner_count.description: Distinct owners the whole policy would resolve. Not truncated, so a client showing only the top few owners can still state how many there are.

owners.description: Policy-wide owner breakdown, ordered by count descending then owner ascending, capped at 100. This is not the per-rule breakdowns summed: each of those is capped independently, so summing them yields neither the real top owners nor a real count.

rules.description: Per-rule projection, index-aligned with the request policy's `rules` array (same length and order). A disabled rule, an unreachable rule, and a rule that could not run all report zero.

apps.description: Per-app rollup of the same projection, present only when the request asks for it with `include_apps=true`. Ordered by resource count descending then name, capped at 200 apps. Resources belonging to no app do not appear — this is a view of the app estate, not of every resource. Empty when the tenant has no apps.

PlatformResourceOwnershipPolicyPreviewRe.title: ResourceOwnershipPolicyPreviewResources
PlatformResourceOwnershipPolicyPreviewRe.description: One page of the resources a candidate policy would attribute to a single owner.

items.description: The page's resources, ordered by `platform_id` so paging is stable.

PlatformOwnershipTagKey.title: OwnershipTagKey
PlatformOwnershipTagKey.description: A tag key the tags ownership rule form can offer, with how much of the estate carries it.

key.description: The tag key, case-folded across the spellings the providers stored. The casing shown is the one most of the tenant's resources use; rule matching folds case, so any spelling of it claims the same resources.

resourceCount.description: Resources carrying this key with a non-blank value, counted once each however many case variants of the key they carry.

PlatformOwnershipTagKeys.title: OwnershipTagKeys
PlatformOwnershipTagKeys.description: Tag keys observed on the tenant's resources, for the tags rule form's autocomplete. These are keys that exist in the data, not keys already configured on a rule.

tagKeys.description: Matching tag keys, most-carried first, capped by `limit`.

session_id.description: Optional session ID to continue an existing session. If omitted, a new session is created.

message.description: The user message to send to the agent orchestrator.

mode.description: Orchestration mode. 0 (default) runs the full AI assistant. 1 is query-writer mode: the agent is narrowed to schema-discovery tools and steered to produce a single ClickHouse SQL statement. Selecting query-writer mode is the frontend's choice (it owns the rollout flag). The mode is sticky per session.

custom_context_ids.description: Optional list of custom context IDs to inject into the agent planner's system prompt for this request. Contexts marked auto_include are always included regardless of this list. Unknown IDs are silently skipped.

app_id.description: Optional app ID to scope the agent's queries to. When set, the agent restricts resource-table queries to resources tagged for this app (via a WHERE clause against the app_memberships table). See docs/apps-topology-principle.md for the architectural framing.

PlatformAgentChatPlanStep.description: A single step in the agent orchestrator's execution plan.

input.description: Raw JSON-encoded input the planner produced for this step (e.g. {"table_name":"aws_ec2_instances"} or {"sql":"SELECT ..."}). Surfaced for traceability when a step fails — lets operators see exactly what the LLM asked an agent to do.

label.description: User-facing caption for this step, the same one the live progress feed carries (e.g. "Running query"). Persisted here so a completed turn's trajectory renders identically to the live view — the feed itself is pruned once the next turn starts.

target.description: Salient input for the step — a table name, search keywords, a truncated SQL statement. Absent when the input carries nothing worth showing.

depends_on.description: Step numbers this step depends on. Populated on plan.steps[]; absent on step_results[].step (where the same shape is reused for traceability).

PlatformAgentChatExecutionPlan.description: The agent orchestrator's execution plan, assembled from the tool-use trajectory.

PlatformAgentChatOutputType.description:
The data type of an agent chat output. Determines which payload field is
populated on `AgentChatOutput` and how the frontend should render the value.

- `query`   — SQL string in `data_str`
- `table`   — `{cols, rows, total_rows?, query?}` in `data_obj`
- `string`  — plain text / markdown in `data_str`
- `object`  — freeform structured record in `data_obj`
- `mermaid` — a validated, sanitized Mermaid diagram string in `data_str`

PlatformAgentChatOutput.description:
A single structured output returned by an agent step. The `type` field
determines which of `data_str` / `data_obj` is populated and how the
frontend should render the payload.

Per-type payload conventions:

- `query`   — `data_str` contains a SQL query string (ClickHouse dialect).
              Returned when an action produced SQL but did not execute it
              (e.g. exploration.execute_query with data access disabled,
              or any flow where the user asked for "just the query").
- `table`   — `data_obj` is `{cols: string[], rows: any[][], total_rows?: number, query?: string}`.
              Returned for tabular data. `query` optionally carries the SQL
              that produced the rows.
- `string`  — `data_str` contains plain text or markdown. Used for prose
              output like diagnose_sync narratives and simple confirmations.
- `mermaid` — `data_str` contains a Mermaid diagram string, already
              syntax-validated and sanitized server-side. Returned by
              mermaid.validate_mermaid_diagram.
- `object`  — `data_obj` is a freeform structured record. The exact shape
              depends on the action and usually mirrors an existing domain
              schema. The per-action payloads currently produced are:


    | Agent | Action | `data_obj` shape |
    |-------|--------|------------------|
    | exploration | `check_syntax` | `{valid: bool, error?: string}` |
    | exploration | `explain_table` | `{table_name, found, plugin?, title?, docs_url?, description?}` |
    | exploration | `search_tables` | `{keywords, plugin?, total_matches, returned, tables: [{table_name, plugin, title?, description?}]}` |
    | summary | `policy_metrics` | `PolicyMetrics` |
    | summary | `environment_overview` | `{synced_table_count, sync_count, syncs_by_status, policy_metrics?}` |
    | remediation | `get_violations` | `{policy_id, policy_name, domain, severity, query_sql, total_violations, columns, rows}` |
    | remediation | `get_policy_context` | `{policy_id, policy_name, description, domain, severity, query_sql, last_evaluated_at?, violation_count, sample_violations}` |
    | policy | `get_policy` | `{id, name, domain, severity, description, query_id, team_name, created_at, updated_at}` |
    | policy | `create_policy` | `{policy_id}` |
    | policy | `update_policy` | `{id, name, domain, severity, description, updated_at}` |
    | policy | `create_policy_group` | `{group_id}` |
    | integration | `get_sync` | `ExpandedSync` (sync metadata + source/destinations/transformers) |
    | integration | `get_sync_run` | `{id, status, status_reason?, failure_reasons?, total_rows, warnings, errors, created_at, completed_at?}` |
    | integration | `create_sync` | `{sync_name}` |
    | integration | `diagnose_sync` | `{sync_name, source_plugin, failed_run_count, total_run_count, failure_patterns}` |


Transport / execution failures (agent unreachable, action returned a Go error, etc.) are surfaced via `step_results[].error` rather than as an `AgentChatOutput`.

data_obj.description: Populated for type=table, object. Shape is documented per-action.

PlatformAgentChatStepResult.description: Outcome of executing a single plan step.

session_id.description: The session ID for this conversation. Use this to continue the session in subsequent requests.

summary.description: LLM-generated summary of the agent results.

total_tokens.description: Total tokens consumed across all LLM calls.

input_tokens.description: Uncached prompt tokens consumed across all LLM calls. The provider bills the three prompt-side counters at different rates, so pricing a request needs all of them; the four token counters sum to total_tokens.

output_tokens.description: Completion tokens produced across all LLM calls.

cache_read_tokens.description: Prompt tokens served from the provider's prompt cache.

cache_write_tokens.description: Prompt tokens written to the provider's prompt cache.

warning.description: Optional warning message indicating token budget or daily limit exceeded. Present only when a limit was exceeded.

refused.description: True when the agent's scope-check guardrail rejected the request as out of scope (off-topic or mixed off-topic) or when the guardrail itself errored and the request was failed-closed. When true, plan and step_results are absent and summary is the canned refusal message.

refusal_reason.description: Short machine-friendly reason populated when refused is true. Either the classifier's reason (e.g. "mixed_off_topic") or "scope_check_error" when the guardrail itself failed.

session_id.description: The newly minted session identifier. Callers should pass this back as `session_id` on subsequent `POST /agent-chat` requests so the orchestrator threads conversation history together.

PlatformAgentChatSessionSummary.description: A single entry in the authenticated user's agent chat session list.

title.description: Short human-readable title generated from the first user message. Omitted (the field is absent, not an empty string) until the first turn has been processed, and also if title generation fails.

created_at.description: When the session was first created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the session's most recent conversation turn. Equals created_at when the session has no turns yet.

PlatformAgentChatSessionList.description: The authenticated user's agent chat conversation sessions.

sessions.description: The user's sessions, most-recently-active first, capped at 50. Empty when the user has no sessions.

PlatformAgentChatSessionTurn.description: A single persisted turn in an agent conversation session.

content.description: For user turns, the user's message. For assistant turns, the final summary text (or canned refusal message when refused is true).

step_results.description: Step outcomes from the execution plan. Absent on user turns and refused turns.

total_tokens.description: Tokens consumed when producing this assistant turn. Zero on user turns and refused turns.

total_latency_ms.description: Wall-clock latency of the original request that produced this assistant turn.

warning.description: Token-budget warning that was surfaced on this assistant turn, if any.

refused.description: True when this assistant turn is the canned refusal from the scope-check guardrail.

refusal_reason.description: Machine-friendly refusal reason; populated when refused is true.

latest.description: True on the most recently persisted turn in the session (regardless of role). At most one turn per response has this set.

PlatformAgentChatSessionHistory.description: The persisted history of an agent conversation session.

title.description: Short human-readable title generated from the first user message. Omitted (the field is absent, not an empty string) until the first turn has been processed, and also if title generation fails.

turns.description: All turns persisted for this session, ordered by sequence ascending. Empty when the session has no turns (or does not exist).

PlatformAgentChatProgressEvent.description: One entry in the live activity feed of an in-flight AI assistant request. `label` is ready to render; `toolkit` / `action` / `target` carry the same information structurally so a client can substitute its own wording.

seq.description: Zero-based position in the request's feed. Monotonic and gap-free; pass the highest value seen back as `after` to fetch only newer events.

kind.description: `started` opens the feed before the assistant begins working. `working` marks a model call in flight — the bulk of a request's duration, during which nothing else is emitted. `thinking` carries the assistant's narration in `detail`. Each tool the assistant uses produces a `tool_started` followed by `tool_completed` or `tool_failed` — a failed tool does not end the request, the assistant can recover from it. `finished` is terminal and is emitted once the request is over, however it ended; its `label` says which ("Done" vs "Failed").

label.description: User-facing caption for this event (e.g. "Running query"). Reads correctly on its own; `target` is optional detail a client may drop.

toolkit.description: Toolkit that owns the action. Absent on non-tool events.

action.description: Action performed (e.g. `execute_query`). Absent on non-tool events.

target.description: Salient input for the call — a table name, search keywords, a truncated SQL statement. Absent when there is nothing worth showing.

detail.description: Long-form text: the assistant's narration on `thinking` events, the error message on `tool_failed`.

step.description: Matches `step` on the plan returned with the completed turn, so the feed can be cross-referenced with the final trajectory. Absent on non-tool events.

PlatformAgentChatProgress.description: The live activity feed for a session's most recent request.

done.description: True once the request is over — not that it succeeded. Clients stop polling on this and read GET /agent-chat/{session_id} to find out how it ended; the terminal event's `label` distinguishes the two ("Done" vs "Failed").

events.description: Events with `seq` greater than the requested `after`, ordered by `seq` ascending. Empty when nothing new has happened, when the session has no recent request, or when the session does not exist.

PlatformTableRow.title: TableRow
PlatformTableRow.description: A single resource row, keyed by column name; each value mirrors its column's type (string, number, boolean, array, nested object, or null). The single-resource detail endpoint (`GET /tables/{table_name}/data/{table_row_id}`) additionally injects a reserved `_cq_apps` key holding the app(s) this resource belongs to: an array of objects shaped `{ "id": <uuid>, "name": <string>, "title": <string>, "owner_team_name": <string|null> }`, where `title` is the resolved display label (server-side COALESCE(title, name)). The array is empty when the resource is unallocated, and may contain more than one app when shared infrastructure is attributed to several apps via topology forward-walk. It also injects a reserved `_cq_environments` key holding the environment names classified onto the resource: an array of strings, empty when environment inference classified nothing, and carrying more than one name when several environment rules claim the resource. It also injects a reserved `_cq_owner` key holding the resource's resolved owner: an object shaped `{ "owner": <string>, "rule_id": <uuid>, "source": <string>, "source_metadata": <object> }`, or `null` when no ownership rule claimed the resource (which is also what a tenant with no ownership policy sees). `source` is the kind of the rule that produced the owner (`static`, `sql` or `tags`) and `source_metadata` is that kind's evidence: `{}` for `static`, the matched tag key for `tags`, the matched column values for `sql`. The list/grid endpoint includes none of the three keys implicitly, and where it shares a name the shape is flatter: it returns `_cq_owner` as a plain string, and `_cq_apps` as an array of app display labels rather than objects, each only when that name is passed in `select`. `_cq_environments` is an array of names on both.

PlatformTableDisplayColumn.title: TableDisplayColumn
PlatformTableDisplayColumn.description:
One entry in the resolved per-table column layout for the UI's column picker.

For the canonical columns (Cloud / Account / Name / Region / Tags) the `id`
is the canonical identifier and `resolved_column` is the physical column it
reads for this table: `_cq_<id>` on a plugin table, which is where the sync
writes the normalized value, and the short form on `cloud_assets` and the
other managed projections, which carry no `_cq_` copy. So the Name column
resolves to `_cq_name` on `aws_route53_hosted_zones` and to `name` on
`cloud_assets`, and the `id` is `name` either way.

For details columns (the resource-specific columns rendered below the fold)
`id` and `resolved_column` are equal — there is no aliasing.

The `/tables/{table_name}/data` and `/tables/{table_name}/columns/{column_name}/values`
endpoints accept either the canonical `id` or a physical column name in
`select`, `sort_by`, `filter` and the column path. A selected canonical
`id` is returned under the name it was requested with.

Stable identifier for this column. Use this in URLs (e.g.
`?select=name`) — the API resolves it to the physical column.

label.description: Human-readable label for the column picker.

resolved_column.description:
Physical column name in the warehouse. May equal `id` (details
columns, and the canonical columns on `cloud_assets`), or differ (the
canonical columns on a plugin table, which read `_cq_*`).

group.description:
`primary` columns are rendered above the fold (the canonical Cloud /
Account / Name / Region / Tags layout). `details` columns are
rendered below in schema order.

PlatformRelatedResourcesTimeBound.description:
The time window that the endpoint applied to one corpus edge.

A few corpus nodes hold an event stream rather than an inventory of
resources — AWS CloudTrail events, GCP audit logs. Their row count grows
with time instead of with the size of the account, so a walk into one is
always narrowed to a window. Every other edge runs unnarrowed and carries
no `time_bound`.

Read `window_days` to learn the window that ran. It is the value asked for
in the request when that value was granted, and the ceiling when it was
more than the endpoint grants.

table_name.description: The event-stream table that the window narrowed.

column.description:
The column the window was applied to. It is the time the event
records, not the time the row was synced.

window_days.description:
The width of the window in days, counted back from the time of the
request. This is the window that ran, which can be smaller than the
`window_days` in the request.

PlatformRelatedResourcesVia.description:
One topology corpus edge that the endpoint walked to build a
related-resources group. `verb` names the relationship. `direction`
says which way the edge was walked to reach the neighbour.

An entry means that the edge ran against the source row without an
error. It does not mean that the edge matched a row. An edge that
matched nothing is still named here, and the group can hold no rows.
Count the related resources from `rows`.

The corpus authors most relationships from one side only, and this
endpoint walks both ways. A group therefore often holds the same verb
twice, with a different direction and weight.

`time_bound` is present only on an edge that touches an event-stream
table, such as AWS CloudTrail events. It names the window that ran. Every
other edge reads all of the data and carries no `time_bound`.

verb.description:
The corpus relationship verb, e.g. `ATTACHES`, `CONTAINS`,
`ENCRYPTED_BY`. Drawn from a closed, curated vocabulary.

direction.description:
How the edge was walked from the source row. `outgoing` follows the
direction in which the corpus authors the edge. `incoming` walks
the edge backwards. The backward walk is what finds a neighbour
whose only authored relationship points at the source, such as a
subnet that reaches its VPC.

salience.description:
The edge's relevance weight in [0, 1] for the direction actually
walked: the forward weight on an `outgoing` edge, the reverse
weight on an `incoming` one. 1.0 is canonical and 0.5 is the
lowest weight this endpoint walks. Use it to rank the entries, or
to choose one verb when a group carries several.

description.description:
The description that the corpus author wrote for this edge, for a
person to read. For example, "An EC2 instance attaches the EBS
volumes referenced in its block_device_mappings entries." The field
is empty when the edge has no description.

PlatformRelatedResourcesByRowGroup.description:
Related-resource rows for one target resource type, coalesced across
every topology corpus edge that lands on this target from the source
row. Rows are deduplicated by `_cq_platform_id` so a target reachable
via multiple edges (e.g. both `ATTACHES` and `HAS_INTERFACE` into
`aws_ec2_network_interfaces`) appears once.

`via` names the corpus edges that the endpoint walked to build this
group, with the verb, the direction of the walk and the weight. It
describes the group and not the individual rows. Because of the
deduplication above, a row that two edges reach cannot be attributed
to one of them.

title.description:
Human-readable display title for the group (e.g. "EC2 EBS
Volumes"). Sourced from the same label registry used by the
rest of the platform UI.

columns.description:
Column layout for the rows below — one entry per element in each
row array, in matching order. Curated labels and render types
come from `shared/displaycolumns` (curated labels for the canonical
columns; humaniser + ClickHouse-type → render-type map for the
rest). Internal `_cq_*` columns appear with `hidden: true`.

rows.description:
Row data. Each row is a positional array aligned with `columns`.
Deduplicated by `_cq_platform_id` across contributing edges.

via.description:
The corpus edges that the endpoint walked for this group, in order
of `salience` from high to low, and then by `verb`. The array is
never empty, because a group exists only where an edge was walked.
More than one entry means that the endpoint reached the neighbour
several ways, and the verbs can differ. An entry does not promise a
matching row. Read `rows` for that.

PlatformRelatedResourcesByRowResponse.description:
Topology-walked related resources for a source row, grouped by target
resource type. Multiple corpus edges into the same target table are
coalesced into a single group with rows deduplicated by
`_cq_platform_id`.

table_name.description: The source table the walk originated from.

display_columns.description:
Resolved per-table column layout for the UI's column picker. See
TableDisplayColumn for how each entry resolves.

PlatformTableColumnName.description: The name of the table column.

value.description: The distinct value of the grouped column. For the `apps` group this is the app's id; drill into a specific app via `filter=_cq_app_id = "<value>"`. The unallocated bucket has an empty value (`_cq_app_id = ""` is rejected as a non-UUID) — drill into it with `filter=_cq_app_id IS EMPTY`. For the `_cq_owner` group this is the owner string; drill in via `filter=_cq_owner = "<value>"`. The unowned bucket has an empty value — drill into it with `filter=_cq_owner IS EMPTY`. For the `_cq_environment` group this is the environment name; drill in via `filter=_cq_environment = "<value>"`. The unclassified bucket has an empty value — drill into it with `filter=_cq_environment IS EMPTY`.

platform_table_filters.name: filter
platform_table_filters.description:
Table filters. This filters the rows that are returned in the result set.

The reserved pseudo-column `_cq_app_id` filters by app membership, e.g. `_cq_app_id = "<uuid>"`. Select multiple apps (union) within a single filter using `_cq_app_id IN ("<uuid>", "<uuid>")` or `_cq_app_id = "<a>" OR _cq_app_id = "<b>"`. Exclude apps with `_cq_app_id != "<uuid>"` or `_cq_app_id NOT IN ("<uuid>", "<uuid>")`, which match resources that do not belong to the named app(s); a negated form must be a standalone filter (not OR/AND-combined). Use `_cq_app_id IS EMPTY` to scope to unallocated resources (those belonging to no app); it cannot be combined with a positive `_cq_app_id` filter. `_cq_app_id` cannot be mixed with other columns inside one filter — combine it with other filters by passing them as separate `filter` parameters, which AND together. It is reserved in CloudQuery's `_cq_` namespace, so it never shadows a plugin's physical `app_id` column.

The reserved pseudo-column `_cq_environment` filters by environment membership the same way, e.g. `_cq_environment = "prod"`, `_cq_environment IN ("prod", "staging")`, `_cq_environment != "prod"`, `_cq_environment NOT IN ("dev", "staging")` and `_cq_environment IS EMPTY` for resources classified into no environment. Environments are identified by NAME (an exact, case-sensitive match on a name the warehouse holds), not by id — unlike apps they have no registry. The same composition rules apply: negated forms must stand alone, `IS EMPTY` cannot be combined with a positive value, and it cannot be mixed with other columns inside one filter. `_cq_app_id` and `_cq_environment` in separate `filter` parameters AND together, so an app and an environment filter compose.

The reserved pseudo-column `_cq_owner` filters by the owner the tenant's ownership rules resolved onto each resource, e.g. `_cq_owner = "platform@example.com"`, `_cq_owner IN ("a@example.com", "b@example.com")`, `_cq_owner != "a@example.com"`, `_cq_owner NOT IN ("a@example.com", "b@example.com")` and `_cq_owner IS EMPTY` for resources no rule claimed. Owners are free-form values produced by the rules (an exact, case-sensitive match), so like environments they have no registry and an empty value is rejected — ask for unowned resources with `IS EMPTY`. The same composition rules apply. A tenant with no ownership policy has no owned resources, so every positive `_cq_owner` filter matches nothing and `_cq_owner IS EMPTY` matches everything. This is the same key the single-resource detail endpoint returns the resolved owner under; the list/grid endpoint accepts it as a filter but does not yet return it on rows.

All three pseudo-columns are filter-only: they resolve through a subquery against a side table rather than a column of the queried table, so passing one to `sort_by` or `group_by` is rejected.

They are honored by the table-data endpoints and by `/tables/{table_name}/columns/{column_name}/grouped`, whichever column is grouped, so a filtered listing and its group counts agree. The remaining endpoints that accept this parameter — ad-hoc and saved query execution, log queries, and distinct column values — treat an unknown column as an error, so passing one there is rejected rather than silently ignored.
